decisionBasis: For the agreed total-harm construct, identical attributable condition loss over the same physical area should not receive an extra premium solely because one ecosystem family has a smaller mapped distribution. Family-relative losses remain visible separately.
weightRule: family weight = fixed mapped family area / fixed total area of the frozen compatible family group
indexRule: index = sum(disjoint cohort area * attributable comparable degradation fraction) / fixed compatible group area
meaning: An extent-weighted, condition-normalized policy index within a declared compatible group. It is not the percentage of all nature destroyed or a measured ecological exchange rate.
conditions: Condition indicators must have a reviewed, common interpretation; the shared percent sign or separate reference-to-collapse normalizations do not prove equivalence.
The ecosystem universe, reference extents, overlap rules and subtype inheritance remain fixed within the method version.

A real area denominator needs harmonized reference boundaries and a reviewed exclusive spatial partition or explicit overlap allocation. Summing mapped source areas alone does not prove a physical union.
Loss of composition, connectivity, function or other material characteristics cannot be silently replaced by one convenient cover or extent metric.
Current condition stock is not multiplied by historical observation length or assumed recovery duration.
An unknown or unassessed family is not zero and is not removed from the denominator.
An unfamiliar ecosystem or incompatible endpoint requires a versioned extension and calibration review before admission.
The current two-family experiment cannot serve as a global nature denominator for the catalogue.
rejectedHiddenPreference: Equal weights across differently sized families give more influence per lost unit area in a smaller mapped family. That may be a defensible conservation preference, but it is not selected implicitly for this total-harm candidate.
limitations: Physical area alone cannot establish ecological importance, biological condition, causality or irreplaceability.

Area weighting can underrepresent unique small ecosystems if uniqueness is part of the desired construct. No automatic uniqueness bonus is included; any such rule would need an explicit method revision.
A cross-family condition exchange remains a TULIP value choice even after indicator and source review. The present synthetic experiment does not validate it.
Nature numerical benchmark thresholds, complete ecosystem coverage and whole-node assessments remain unfinished.
